detail.overview:
Are you ready to build AI that doesn’t just recognise words, but understands the importance of tone?

Fongbe is the most widely spoken local language in southern Benin, with around 2.3 million native speakers. It is a tonal language: a single wrong tone mark can change the meaning of a word, or of a whole sentence. Yet automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems for African tonal languages still often drop or misplace tones, so their transcripts can look plausible while saying something different. Without reliable, tone-aware speech technology, Fongbe speakers remain largely shut out of voice-based digital services.

In this challenge, your objective is to build an automatic speech recognition model that transcribes spoken Fongbe into correctly spelled, fully tone-marked text. You will train on about 350 hours of transcribed speech of mixed quality (validated recordings from many voices, recordings with uncertain tone annotation, and Bible readings), and your model must run on a single CPU thread.

Your solution will show that accurate, tone-aware speech recognition does not need expensive hardware. A frugal Fongbe model could run on low-cost devices and local servers, bringing voice-based public services, information and education to all Fongbe speakers. The winning approaches could also guide speech recognition for other tonal languages across Benin and West Africa.

This challenge is open to all and is organised in partnership with Benin’s Ministry of Digital Transformation and Innovation (MTDI), which leads the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, the Agency for Information Systems and Digital Affairs (ASIN) and the Institute for Inclusive Digital Africa (IIDiA), as part of the J’aime Ma Langue project.

Organised by the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Innovation (MTDI, Ministère de la Transformation Digitale et de l'Innovation, en charge de la Stratégie nationale d'intelligence artificielle) of Benin, in charge of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, with the Agency for Information Systems and Digital Affairs (ASIN, Agence des Systèmes d'Information et du Numérique) and the Institute for Inclusive Digital Africa (IIDiA), as part of the J'aime Ma Langue project funded by the Gates Foundation.

The Ministry of Digital Transformation and Innovation (MTDI, Ministère de la Transformation Digitale et de l'Innovation, en charge de la Stratégie nationale d'intelligence artificielle) leads Benin's digital policy and is in charge of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy. With the Agency for Information Systems and Digital Affairs (ASIN, Agence des Systèmes d'Information et du Numérique) and the Institute for Inclusive Digital Africa (IIDiA), it carries J'aime Ma Langue, the national project that gives a voice to the languages of Benin and opens the doors of the digital world to those who are still kept away from it.…
detail.evaluation:
The evaluation metric for this challenge is Weighted Word Error Rate, which measures the accuracy of predicted transcriptions against the ground truth. WER calculates the number of word substitutions, deletions and insertions required to transform a prediction into the correct transcription. Each transcription is weighted according to the square root of its reference word count, giving longer transcriptions greater influence on the final score. The final score is calculated by dividing the sum of weighted word errors by the sum of transcription weights. Lower scores are better, with a score of 0 indicating perfect transcriptions.

Scoring on syllables. The metric is applied to syllables instead of words. The ground truth has been split into tone-marked syllables with the public function syllabify(); you must apply the same function to your transcriptions before submitting. It normalises the text, splits each word into syllables and writes each tone as a digit (for example, "Un nɔ́ ɖu nǔ" becomes "un nɔ1 ɖu nu3"), so that a tone error costs one syllable rather than a whole word, and tones survive any text cleaning. Submissions that are not syllabified will score poorly.

Solution deployment and compute requirements

- Training is unconstrained (GPUs allowed). 

- 
Inference must be frugal: the solutions are meant to run in production on modest CPU servers and mobile devices. The limits below are eliminatory, not part of the score: the ranking is the syllable WER alone, but a solution above a limit cannot win a prize. They apply to the complete system, from audio to tone-marked transcription.

Size on disk: at most 1000 MB for all the weights of the system, pretrained models and language model included, after any quantisation.

detail.data_or_tools:
This challenge provides approximately 370 hours of Fongbe speech data, including recordings from multiple speakers, domains and recording conditions. The dataset includes both high-quality, linguist-validated transcriptions and recordings with less reliable tone annotations, giving participants an opportunity to explore how best to learn from data of varying quality.
Skills: Automatic Speech Recognition, Natural Language Processing, Multilingual AI
detail.eligibility:
Languages and tools: You may only use open-source languages and tools in building models for this challenge.
Who can compete: Open to all
This challenge is open to all.
Datasets, packages and general principles
The solution must use publicly-available, open-source packages only.
Note that to count, your submission must first pass processing. If your submission fails during the processing step, it will not be counted and not receive a score; nor will it count against your daily submission limit. If you encounter problems with your submission file, your best course of action is to ask for advice on the challenge page.
The winners will be paid via bank transfer, PayPal if payment is less than or equivalent to $100, or other international money transfer platform. International transfer fees will be deducted from the total prize amount, unless the prize money is under $500, in which case the international transfer fees will be covered by Zindi. In all cases, the winners are responsible for any other fees applied by their own bank or other institution for receiving the prize money. All taxes imposed on prizes are the sole responsibility of the winners.…

Individual entry

detail.submission:
Submission Limits: 10 submissions per day, 300 submissions overall.
Public-Private Split: Zindi maintains a public leaderboard and a private leaderboard for each challenge. The Public Leaderboard includes approximately 30% of the test dataset. The private leaderboard will be revealed at the close of the challenge and contains the remaining 70% of the test set.
Code Review: Top 10 on the private leaderboard will receive an email requesting their code at the close of the challenge. You will have 48 hours to submit your code.
You may participate in challenges as an individual or in a team of up to four people. When creating a team, the team must have a total submission count less than or equal to the maximum allowable submissions as of the formation date. A team will be allowed the maximum number of submissions for the challenge, minus the total number of submissions among team members at team formation. Prizes are transferred only to the individual players or to the team leader.
Multiple accounts per user are not permitted, and neither is collaboration or membership across multiple teams. Individuals and their submissions originating from multiple accounts will be immediately disqualified from the platform.
